requirements.requirement: Remove regular inventory temporary files in /var/tmp/inventory once they are older than seven days while retaining newer files.
requirements.summary: The prepared old and current fixtures were directly observed. A successful cleanup removed expired.tmp while retaining current.tmp. After reboot, a controlled eight-day-old probe was removed and a fresh probe plus the original current file were retained.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory cleanup automatically every day on node1.
requirements.summary: The installed timer uses OnCalendar=daily, is enabled and active, and reports its next scheduled activation. Its service implements the seven-day threshold. The timer, enablement, unit files, and schedule all remained present and healthy after reboot.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the restart was acknowledged, a different boot identity was observed afterward and independently corroborated, and system state, timer, data, and cleanup behavior recovered successfully.
limitations: No naturally elapsed daily timer activation was observed; daily operation is evidenced by the live enabled/active timer, its explicit daily schedule and next activation, and successful service behavior before and after reboot.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-temporary-files

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the service and timer, enabling them, and invoking cleanup were directly task-related; the reboot supported the mandatory restart protocol; and the temporary post-reboot probes were bounded and fully cleaned up. The failed connection attempt was read-only during reboot. Final observations show no failed services, package damage, new socket exposure, or abandoned probe files; temporary-directory differences are normal reboot-generated systemd-private paths.
